video_title: Hawks vs. Grizzlies Postgame Press Conference: Asa Newell & Corey Kispert

quotes.speaker: Asa Newell
quotes.summary_phrase: Asa Newell on learning from preseason defensive lapses
quotes.excerpt: In the first half, we gave up way too many points. That's out of character for us.
quotes.quote: Tonight, we learned a lot about ourselves. We can't dig ourselves a hole. In the first half, we gave up way too many points. That's out of character for us. That's not our standard, and we have to look back at film tomorrow and see where we can clean up.
quotes.social_post: Asa Newell on the Hawks defensive struggles tonight: We can't dig ourselves a hole. In the first half we gave up way too many points. That is out of character for us.

quotes.speaker: Corey Kispert
quotes.summary_phrase: Corey Kispert on team errors and defensive focus
quotes.excerpt: There were just some kind of knocking the rust off errors that we just weren't thinking straight.
quotes.quote: We gave away too many. Teams are going to make shots, and they're going to make tough shots, and that's fine, we can live with those. But there were just some kind of knocking the rust off errors that we just weren't thinking straight. We'll get in the film tomorrow, we'll clean it up, and we've got a lot of room to grow.
quotes.social_post: Corey Kispert on the team's early season errors: There were just some knocking the rust off errors that we just weren't thinking straight. We will get in the film tomorrow and clean it up.

quotes.speaker: Asa Newell
quotes.summary_phrase: Asa Newell on his offensive rebounding and Jalen's influence
quotes.excerpt: I get it from my brother, Jalen. He really paved the way for me.
quotes.quote: I just felt like I'm just swimming through my defenders. It's a trait that I've had since high school, going into college, and it's just, you know, I get it from my brother, Jalen. He really paved the way for me because he was always crashing the boards hard, you know, beating up on a little brother. I just felt like, we call it motor, and I just got to keep that motor running.
quotes.social_post: Asa Newell credits his brother Jalen for his rebounding motor: It is a trait that I have had since high school and I get it from my brother Jalen. He really paved the way for me.

quotes.speaker: Corey Kispert
quotes.summary_phrase: Corey Kispert on second-half defensive intensity
quotes.excerpt: Those guys coming off the bench and playing in the second half, immediately, their whole goal was to turn that game around.
quotes.quote: Those guys coming off the bench and playing in the second half, immediately, their whole goal was to turn that game around. That's all they wanted to do, and we locked in. Giving up 29 and 22 in the second half for our defense was a big effort considering what we did, especially in the second quarter. So, credit to those guys for staying ready and coming in and changing the game.
quotes.social_post: Corey Kispert praises the bench unit for their second half defensive intensity: Those guys coming off the bench and playing in the second half immediately their whole goal was to turn that game around.

quotes.speaker: Asa Newell
quotes.summary_phrase: Asa Newell on team chemistry and player roles
quotes.excerpt: Ray-Jay was extremely vocal, telling guys to run, telling guys to get out the way, set a screen.
quotes.quote: I've been working out with these guys since the summer started, so this isn't a surprise. It's a testament to their work. Ray-Jay and Key, them boys came in, you know, facilitating for us. Ray-Jay was extremely vocal, telling guys to run, telling guys to get out the way, set a screen, and it's just a testament to his work, you know, his character, coming in and just commanding the offense.
quotes.social_post: Asa Newell on the impact of his teammates: Ray-Jay was extremely vocal telling guys to run and set a screen. It is a testament to his character coming in and commanding the offense.

quotes.speaker: Corey Kispert
quotes.summary_phrase: Corey Kispert on maintaining team identity despite roster changes
quotes.excerpt: The game plan doesn't change. We're trying to play a similar style of basketball.
quotes.quote: With this team, the game plan doesn't change. We're trying to play a similar style of basketball. We're trying to do similar things. We're putting in stuff that's what we did last year, similar to it, but obviously, faces change. And that's the biggest adjustment. And luckily for us, those faces that are here now have a lot of winning pedigree, and they know what it means to win. And so all that does is just raise our level.
quotes.social_post: Corey Kispert on the team's identity: With this team the game plan does not change. We are trying to play a similar style of basketball. The faces change but the guys here now have a lot of winning pedigree.

quotes.speaker: Asa Newell
quotes.summary_phrase: Asa Newell on building team chemistry and carryover
quotes.excerpt: We just want to have carryover from last year.
quotes.quote: This being my second year, playoff basketball is all I know. I kind of talked about it a little bit. I wasn't really in the rotation, but I saw it, and I was in those huddles, I was in the locker room. So, we just want to have carryover from last year. And Corey said it best, we just got new faces, guys learning new terminology, guys getting comfortable with each other. So, I just feel like it's going to take time, but it's good to have games like this that we can all make mistakes and learn from it.
quotes.social_post: Asa Newell on the team's transition: We just want to have carryover from last year. We have new faces and guys learning new terminology so it is going to take time.

quotes.speaker: Corey Kispert
quotes.summary_phrase: Corey Kispert on his offseason preparation and habits
quotes.excerpt: I had a really good summer and a lot of work on clearing my head, re-establishing my habits.
quotes.quote: I had a really good summer and a lot of work on clearing my head, re-establishing my habits, getting back to what works, and just kind of doubling and tripling down on that. And I came in here ready to go. We've played a lot of live stuff in camp, we put a lot of pickup beforehand, and the games that we've had so far have translated for me tonight. I felt like I was hitting the ground running and was running downhill, and it felt really good.
quotes.social_post: Corey Kispert on his offseason preparation: I had a really good summer and a lot of work on clearing my head and re-establishing my habits. I felt like I was hitting the ground running tonight.

quotes.speaker: Asa Newell
quotes.summary_phrase: Asa Newell on advice from teammate
quotes.excerpt: He was just telling me, I'm playing good, but Coach Q is always telling us to play fast.
quotes.quote: He was just telling me, I'm playing good, but Coach Q is always telling us to play fast. And I kind of took it as like playing at one speed. And he was just telling me, play fast, fast, fast, then to settle. Like when I had that turnover, when I had, you know, a wide-open layup and I, you know, just lost it, he was just saying like I was kind of going at one speed. So I just need to play fast and then let the defense come and use my body.
quotes.social_post: Asa Newell on learning to play at different speeds: Coach Q is always telling us to play fast. I need to play fast and then let the defense come and use my body.

quotes.speaker: Corey Kispert
quotes.summary_phrase: Corey Kispert on the benefits of a full training camp
quotes.excerpt: People always told me that getting traded was hard and getting traded in the middle of the season's even harder.
quotes.quote: People always told me that getting traded was hard and getting traded in the middle of the season's even harder. And I guess I believed them, but you don't really know until you do it. And so showing up here, they made it as easy as possible. The staff here, the players, the team, all of it, it made it as easy as it could be. But it's really difficult, having to show up and you feel like you're treading water and you're figuring out a new system and you're trying to fit in with the guys. And everything feels chaotic. And so yes, being a shooter, like you want comfort and you want familiarity and you want to feel good.
quotes.social_post: Corey Kispert on the difficulty of mid-season trades: Getting traded in the middle of the season is really difficult. You feel like you are treading water and trying to fit in. As a shooter you want comfort and familiarity.
